newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT -Motorola second quarter results.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT -Motorola second quarter results.

text.p: Motorola Inc reported higher 1997 second quarter earnings before a previously announced charge taken to cover costs of exiting a lower performing business and said it continues to review its business segments. All business segments, including semiconductor and cellular products, contributed to the second quarter gains.
A full text of the news release follows.

SCHAUMBURG, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--July 8, 1997--Motorola, Inc. today reported sales of $7.5 billion in the second quarter of 1997, up 10.0 percent from $6.8 billion a year earlier. In the first half, sales rose 2.7 percent to $14.2 billion from $13.8 billion in the first half of 1996.

As a result of the decision, announced last week, to phase out its participation in the dynamic random access memory (DRAM) market and the associated charge against pre-tax earnings of $170 million or 18 cents per share, second quarter earnings were $268 million or 44 cents per share, compared with $326 million or 54 cents per share a year earlier. Earnings in the first six months were $593 million or 97 cents per share, compared with $710 million or $1.17 per share in last year's first half, with the comparison again affected by the $170 million or 18 cents per share charge noted above. The per share comparisons are on a fully diluted basis per common and common equivalent share.
Net margin on sales was 3.6 percent in the second quarter, compared with 4.8 percent a year ago, while the first half net margin was 4.2 percent against 5.1 percent in the year-earlier period.

Robert L. Growney, president and chief operating officer, said, "Excluding the effect of the second quarter charge related to phasing out participation in the DRAM market, we achieved increased profitability on a quarter-to-quarter basis versus the prior year. Also, each of our business segments reported increased sales and orders.

The Semiconductor and Cellular Products segments both showed improvement over the growth rates reported for the first quarter, while the Land Mobile Products segment continues to experience very good growth."
Growney reviewed the following results of Motorol's major operations for the seocnd quarter, compared with the second quarter of 1996:
Cellular Products Segment

Segment sales rose 6 percent to $2.8 billion and orders rose 20 percent. Operating profits were flat, but would have declined except for a small gain from the sale of two investments. The segment includes results of the Cellular Subscriber Sector (CSS), the Cellular Infrastructure Group (CIG) and the Network Management Group. CSS sales increased, led by Asia-Pacific, China and Europe, while they were unchanged in Pan America and declined in both Japan and South Korea. Orders increased significantly led by Asia-Pacific, China, Europe and Pan America while they declined in Japan and South Korea. Sales and orders for Global System for Mobile Communications (GSM) based digital products were very significantly higher.

During the second quarter CSS commenced shipments of the GSM1900 digital StarTAC(TM) cellular phone for the U.S. market, and the International 8800, the world's first dual band 900 and 1800 megahertz (MHz) GSM digital phone. CSS also introduced and shipped a new lower-tier digital offering, the GSM StarTAC(TM) 70.

In the quarter, Motorola's newest wearable phone, the StarTAC(TM) 8600 Designer Series phone featuring the VoiceNote(TM) recording function and Caller Identification Display, was made commercially available to Signature dealer locations across the United States.

Motorola was one of the companies selected by Japan's NTT Mobile Communications Network, Inc. to develop cellular telephones for its next generation wideband Code Division Multiple Access (CDMA) digital system.

CIG sales increased slightly, as higher sales in the Pan American and Asia-Pacific regions were largely offset by lower sales in Europe and Japan. Sales were lower in Japan due to the migration from existing technology to CDMA, in which CIG announced a major award for a nationwide system in the first quarter of 1997. Orders increased, led by the Pan American region, Japan and the Asia-Pacific region, while they declined in Europe.

CIG was selected to deploy CDMA systems in Georgia and Virginia, and announced the commercial launch of its CDMA system in Albuquerque, N.M. Commercially deployed Motorola CDMA systems now total 23 worldwide.
The group also won contracts totaling more than $145 million to expand existing GSM systems in China and Kuwait.

CIG won a contract worth more than $200 million to supply Total Access Coverage System (TACS) analog cellular infrastructure equipment and services in China. The group also announced more than $100 million in TACS expansion contracts in the Chinese provinces of Shandong and Jiangsu.

In Brazil, TELEPAR awarded CIG a $132 million contract to expand the existing Advanced Mobile Phone System (AMPS) analog cellular infrastructure systems covering 58 cities. Semiconductor Products Segment

Segment sales were up 3 percent to $2.0 billion, and orders rose 36 percent. The segment reported an operating loss versus a profit a year ago. Excluding the impact of charges related to phasing out participation in the DRAM market, operating profits would have increased.

In deciding to phase out of the DRAM market, the sector announced that it plans to reallocate resources to other technologies, including proprietary fast static random access memories (FSRAM) and integrated memories such as flash and electrically erasable programmable read-only memory (EEPROM).

Orders increased significantly in the Asia-Pacific region, Europe and the Americas, and were higher in Japan. Among market segments, communications posted the highest order growth as all end markets had higher orders. Distributor orders also improved. Among key product segments, orders increased significantly in all categories except memories, which had significantly lower orders.
The sector was reorganized into five specific market groups -- Networking & Computer Systems, Wireless Subscriber Systems, Transportation Systems, Consumer Systems, and Semiconductor Components.

Motorola and Eastman Kodak announced they will jointly develop sensors for digital imaging using complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) technology. This advanced CMOS imager technology will enable the design of smaller, lighter cameras with longer battery life.

The sector shipped its 2 billionth 68HC05 8-bit microcontroller. The sector also announced the industry's first 300MHz volume desktop and portable microprocessor. It is part of the PowerPC(TM) 603e microprocessor family.
Land Mobile Products Segment
Segment sales rose 22 percent to $1.2 billion. Orders increased 30 percent and operating profits were higher.

Orders for iDEN(TM) equipment for Integrated Digital Enhanced Networks were up significantly, including more than $300 million from Nextel Communications, Inc. for the continued rollout of its nationwide network in the U.S. and more than $50 million from McCaw International for systems in Brazil and Argentina. Avantel, a Motorola joint venture in Colombia, announced the commercial launch of an iDEN system in Bogota with expansion plans for five additional cities.

Major system awards in the U.S. included orders from Henrico County, Va., Belmont County, Ohio, and Tallahassee and Pinellas Counties in Florida. Other system awards were received for a major public safety system expansion in Colombia; a railroad system in Brazil; utility, public safety and government systems in Mexico; petroleum and government systems in Russia; as well as systems in the Middle East and Africa, the United Kingdom and France. Orders also were received for specialized mobile radio system (SMRS) equipment from Moscow Telephone Company and for portable and mobile trunked radios from South African Airways.

Several new products were introduced including the GM950 Select 5 two-way mobile radio in Europe; the Mobile Workstation 520, which provides the power of a desktop computer for in-vehicle use; the VersiTAC(TM) integrated wireless data solution, which offers customized, seamless wireless solutions on public or integrated (private/public) data networks; and an expanded line of CENTRALINK 911(TM) products for the emergency dispatch market.
Messaging, Information and Media Segment
Segment sales increased 6 percent to $1.1 billion, orders rose 1 percent, and operating profits were higher.

Orders in the Paging Group were flat, while orders increased in the Information Systems Group. The Paging Group again experienced significantly lower sales and orders from North American paging operators. Management believes that these operators continue to control inventories tightly in order to improve their financial positions and cash flow. Paging orders were up significantly in all international markets except Japan, where orders were lower.
The Advanced Messaging Group received a major award from PageNet for one-way, two-way and voice paging infrastructure through 1999.

Motorola's Wireless Messaging System was chosen to support Taiwan's island-wide paging network under a contract with First International Telecom, a paging operator in Taiwan. Automotive, Energy and Components Sector
Sector sales increased 6 percent, orders were 13 percent higher, and operating profits were lower. The sector's results are reported as part of the "Other Products" segment.

Orders increased in each of the sector's business units. The Energy Products Division had the highest rate of order growth as demand increased for rechargeable batteries and battery chargers. Orders in the Components Product Group increased for printed circuit boards from both external and internal customers. The Automotive and Industrial Electronics Group was awarded business from U.S. automotive manufacturers for body electronics and engine control units, and received awards for two automotive body electronics programs from a major European manufacturer.
Space and Systems Technology Group

Group sales increased 94 percent and orders were up 187 percent compared with the second quarter of 1996, when order booking was delayed pending completion of a short-term credit facility being negotiated by Iridium LLC. The group reported a profit compared with a loss in the year-earlier period. The group's results are reported as part of the "Other Products" segment.

Depreciation expense in the second quarter declined as a percent of sales to 7.6 percent from 8.4 percent in the year-earlier period, as a result of decreased fixed asset expenditures in 1996. The tax rate for the second quarter was 35 percent, the same as the year-earlier period. The tax rate for the full year 1996 was also 35 percent. Review and Outlook

Christopher B. Galvin, chief executive officer, said, "Motorola continues to build for the future by redirecting resources to development programs with the greatest potential, while focusing on core technology platforms. Evidence of improved performance ranges from order patterns in our semiconductor business to the growing acceptance of CDMA, iDEN(TM), advanced messaging and other wireless communications technologies. The successful launch of 12 IRIDIUM(R) satellites during the quarter underscores our confidence in the possibilities of global satellite communications," he said.

"Motorola's presence is strengthening in emerging markets throughout the world, especially in Latin America. Continued stable growth in the United States, along with improving economic conditions in markets such as Europe and Japan, give Motorola an exciting range of opportunities for solid growth in profitability," he said.

"Our review of development programs that have not lived up to their promise is continuing," Galvin said, "and we have already taken actions as a result of that process, despite the negative impact of such charges on quarterly financial results.

The potential for further actions could result in additional charges against earnings in the second half of the year. We will continue to position the company for sustainable long-term growth and profitability."
Business Risks:

The statements in "Review and Outlook" and about reallocating resources in connection with the decision to phase out of the DRAM market, deployment and commercialization of IRIDIUM(R) services, the Iridium LLC financing negotiations and any other statements that are not historical facts are forward-looking and involve risks and uncertainties. Product and technology development and commercialization risks and uncertainties, including for new digital technologies, newer messaging services and integrated radio digital products, IRIDIUM products and services, and flat panel displays; the success of establishing technology platforms throughout the world; the ability of the semiconductor business to sustain a rebound worldwide and Motorola's ability to capitalize on that rebound and to compete; the success of strategic decisions to improve performance; the ability of Motorola to contain costs and charges against earnings as a result of any actions to improve performance; unforeseen costs in connection with the decision to phase out of the DRAM market; pricing of DRAM products during the market exit period; continued weak demand for paging products in North America; the outcome of Iridium LLC financing negotiations; steady growth in emerging markets; and the factors in Motorola's Form 10-K/A in Item 7 on pages 14 and 15 and in its other SEC filings are among some of the factors that could cause Motorola's results to differ materially from those in the forward-looking statements.
